title: Arcade Snack Rush: Crew Drill

selected_categories.reasoning: The player repeatedly takes orders, cooks one of several dishes, serves customers, and manages the kitchen loop directly. Cooking and service execution are the most obvious moment-to-moment mechanics.
Money is reinvested into tables, extra room space, supplies, and staff. The game strongly emphasizes venue expansion, throughput growth, and semi-automated business scaling.

The player physically moves around the venue and interacts with kitchen stations such as the grill, sink, and trash in real time. It is simplified and arcade-like, but still simulates a small operational kitchen workflow.
Ingredients, dish capacity, money, payroll, and room ownership all constrain progress. Efficient balancing of these systems is necessary to maintain service flow and fund upgrades.
Recruiting staff, upgrading productivity, paying wages, and unlocking more profitable space create a recognizable tycoon progression arc, though the game remains more hands-on than a pure tycoon.

uncertainty_notes: The arcade theme could suggest other categories, but the implemented mechanics are much closer to cooking/service management than to arcade action genres.
Cooking simulator and Restaurant tycoon are both strong matches; their ordering depends on whether direct play loop or longer-term progression is weighted more heavily.
Automation through staff is meaningful, but the game remains too active and tactile to classify as an idle strategy or clicker game.
